title: Keep every team's migration on the safe path

blocks.text: Every service applies its schema migrations on start. `Migrations.Migration` is the class each team extends, and each subclass writes the statements of one change. Three incidents this quarter came from the same place:

items: a team overrode `apply` to log timings, dropped the history check, and its change ran twice on the next deploy;
a deploy script called `migrate` on a migration it had loaded and ran the change with nobody holding the lock;
a change that failed halfway left the history locked, and every later deploy refused to start.

blocks.text: Finish `src/main/java/practice/Migrations.java` so that a migration runs its change at most once per database and only while holding the history's lock, a change that throws is not recorded and releases the lock, and none of the three incidents can be repeated by a team's subclass or by code that holds a migration. Teams write their subclasses in their own packages and must keep being able to. About ten lines in total, most of them in `apply`.

cases.says: pending migrations run their statements in order, are recorded, and leave the history unlocked
a migration whose version is already recorded runs nothing
while another deploy holds the lock, a migration runs nothing and fails
no subclass can replace the sequence that applies a migration
a migration's change is reachable by subclasses but not by callers, so callers can only run it through apply
a migration whose change throws is not recorded as applied, and the exception reaches the caller
a migration whose change throws leaves the history unlocked for the next deploy

origin.section: A Class Open to Subclassing Needs a Final Skeleton and Protected Hooks; Otherwise Make It final

concepts: A class open to subclassing keeps the sequence and its rules in a final method and lets subclasses fill in protected hooks, so no subclass can skip the rules and no caller can run a step on its own.
The skeleton's rules include what happens when a hook throws, so its cleanup goes in a finally.
